claims.text: Copying a step from another service copies its mistakes and old defaults too; asking the keeper of a shared file puts each step in that person's queue.
A platform is run as a product for internal users: judged by whether teams choose it and by the four delivery measures (lead time, change failure rate among them), not by how many tools it holds.

service-footprint.sh searches only CI, deploy/, Compose and its DB setup, the Caddyfile and lab/devops scripts (never docs or tests); each file naming the service, ignoring case, gets an area by path; a deploy/ file is a NetworkPolicy if a line starts 'kind: NetworkPolicy'.

platform-capabilities.md lists OpenTofu's cluster and platform layers, Argo CD and the config repo, Gateway and HTTPRoute, Sealed Secrets, the require-image-digest admission policy, CI jobs image/publish and manifests, staging Prometheus and a template plus script for new services.

Self-service per the table: deploy via PR to the config repo yes; admission policy yes (nothing to do if manifest has digest); route and new Secret partly (keeper reviews / seal-secrets.sh lists each Secret); CI image/publish and staging Prometheus no.
Steps not yet self-service include adding the service's app label to each shared NetworkPolicy (database, RabbitMQ, Keycloak), because each policy lists every label it lets in.

The lead's conditional view: with one team, three .NET services and a new service every few quarters, no separate group is needed yet; it changes when two or more product teams repeat the steps or requests to the keepers queue.
In Đơn Hàng a team deploys by committing its overlay to the config repository through a pull request, and Argo CD syncs it and corrects the cluster when it drifts from Git.

claims.text: Trade-offs: copying costs nothing up front but copies mistakes; asking the keeper costs the keeper's time per service; written steps fit one team adding a service every few quarters; a separate group fits several teams repeating steps.

Choices: one team, rare services → keep table and steps current; a second team waiting on the same keeper → start with the 'no' rows both wait on and watch lead time; a portal proposal → ask which 'no'/'partly' row it turns into 'yes'.
